summary:
Independent review of Liao Shi ch. 042 owned units s0001–s0010, s0236, s0228–s0235, and s0011–s0019. No owned unit states a birth, death, or age, so none was treated as omitted life data; s0012’s 大明七年癸卯 is a calendrical epoch constant, not a personal vital date. Each dated claim was assigned to the named person’s own act: Taizong’s Datong 1 collection (AD 947); Ma Chongji’s Jin Tianfu 4 presentation (AD 939); Wang Bai and Li Zheng’s Yingli 11 submission (AD 961); Jia Jun’s Tonghe 12 presentation (AD 994) with posting only onOrBefore 994; Shengzong’s adoption/promulgation in that same Tonghe 12; Zu Chongzhi’s Daming 6 presentation (AD 462). Conventional reign-year labels were converted against the Chinese plus calendar tables (ruler, polity, era). 宋武帝大明六年 is a Liao Shi temple-name slip for Xiaowu’s 大明; 462 is still supported for Zu by the era count and by s0012 癸卯 = Daming 7 / AD 463, while p010 remains undated. Shen Yue is an undated retrospective Song Shu witness. Context 504/510 rows stay posthumous and do not feed p001 hints. Active hints match those personal events. All owned checks supported; findings empty.
Independent review of 遼史卷42 owned units s0020–s0047 against the sealed Chinese text only. These twenty-eight units are Daming-calendar (大明曆) computational constants and algorithms: 日法、餘數、歲餘、沒分、沒法、周天、虛分、行分法、小分法、通周、會周、通法、差率, then 推朔術 (including 上元年數、閏餘、積月、積日、大小餘、天正十一月朔、月大小), 求次月, 求弦望, and the 推閏術 heading. unitPeople is empty for every owned unit; ownedItems and ownedPeople are empty, so itemChecks and personChecks are empty by assignment. No named person appears as owner of a dated event. No birth, death, age, or personal life-date is present or omitted. Mentions of 上元、甲子、天正十一月朔, and remainder thresholds (閏餘二百四十七以上、小餘千八百四十九以上) are procedural inputs and sexagenary naming rules for a sought year, not a person’s own event and not a Gregorian event date. The epoch span 上元甲子至宋大明七年癸卯 lives in context unit s0012, which this job does not own. No active-date hints exist to test. No conversion, bound, or reception issue arises. Chronology support for this slice is vacuously complete.
Independent review of Liaoshi ch. 042 owned units s0048–s0075 against the sealed Chinese text only. The span is computational calendar procedure: intercalation from 閏餘/章歲/閏法 and the no-中氣 rule; twenty-four qi from 入上元年數 with 紀法 remainders named from 甲子 to 天正十一月冬至, then successive qi by adding 15 days plus listed 小餘/小分; 土王用事 offsets from winter solstice; 沒/滅 from winter-solstice 小餘; solar lodge from 朔積日 named from 虛一 at 天正十一月朔夜半, with long/short-month and 行分 steps; lunar lodge from 朔小餘×124/860. Context units s0038/s0045–s0047 and s0076–s0078 are likewise anonymous algorithm steps. No personal names, kinship, ages, births, deaths, accessions, or dated life events appear. 上元 is the calendar epoch parameter, 天正十一月/冬至/朔 are civil-month computational targets, 虛 is lodge Void, and 土王/沒/滅 are technical terms—not persons or commemorations. unitPeople is empty on every owned and adjoining unit; ownedItems and ownedPeople are empty, so no item or person checks are due. Nothing here supplies a personal date window or an active-life hint. No omitted birth, death, age, or personal date-context was found, and no competing biographical readings arise. Findings are empty.
Independent review of Liaoshi ch. 042 owned units s0076–s0079 and s0081–s0105 against the sealed Chinese only. These passages are calendrical-computational: subtracting a computed quantity from the new-moon midnight solar lodge to obtain the moon's lodge; long/short-month increments; the 遲疾歷 entry algorithm (通法/通周, 天正十一月朔夜半 naming, cycle drop at 27 days + remainder 14631); true-sun lodge adjustments by 損益/盈縮; and the 陰陽歷 header plus days 1–9 of 損益率兼數. unitPeople is empty for every owned unit. No personal name, birth, death, age, accession, or historically dated life event appears. 天正十一月 in s0084 is a procedural epoch for midnight sequence entry, not a dated biographical occurrence. 一日益十六 through 九日損六七十 are sequence-row labels, not civil dates. s0081 is an editorial pointer to printed tables (pp. 522–524), not a source date. ownedItems and ownedPeople are empty, so there are no item or person chronology claims to endorse or correct, and no active-date hints to test. Nothing in the owned span was omitted that would require a birth, death, age, westernBounds, or reception event. The supplied sourceUrl was requested for confirmation and returned HTTP 404; the verdict rests on the sealed unit texts, not on a live page or on the English glosses.
Independent review of Liaoshi chapter 042 owned units s0106–s0110 and s0119–s0141 against the sealed Chinese only (the supplied chinesenotes URL returned 404 and was not treated as a witness). These 28 units are consecutive computational matter from the calendar treatise: s0106–s0110 continue a day-index 損益/兼數 table for 十日 through 十四日, and s0119–s0141 give the 推入陰陽歷術 chain through 求次月/次日, 朔望差, 合朔月食 limits, 定大小餘, 加時 (命以子), and 月去日道度. No anthroponym, birth, death, age, reign-year life date, or personal event appears. 天正十一月朔 is a recurring winter-solstice-month epoch used to name a midnight sequence entry, not a dated biographical occurrence; 子 is the first earthly-branch double-hour, not a person. ownedItems and ownedPeople are empty and match the source. Neighbor units s0103–s0105, s0142–s0144, and s0051 were read only as context and likewise yield no owned personal chronology. No item or person check applies; no omitted life date or date-context finding is warranted.
Independent review of owned units s0142–s0145 and s0147–s0170 in 遼史卷四十二《曆象志上》. Every owned unit is calendrical or planetary-computation text: lunar-latitude remainder grades (少、半、太、強), yang/yin inside-outside, the 測景漏刻中星 header plus a modern-edition table locator, dusk/dawn culmination-star procedure, five-planet rates, and Jupiter and Mars synodic-motion parameters. No named person appears in any owned unit, matching empty unitPeople. Day counts such as 十六日、二十八日、百一十二日、三百九十八日、七十二日 are visibility and synodic durations, not historical event dates of a person. 天正朔 and 虛一 are computational naming epochs, not accession or life dates. 〈（見書529－531頁有表）〉 is a printed-edition page note, not a Liao-period date. ownedItems and ownedPeople are empty; there is no claim or person chronology to check, and the Chinese does not omit a birth, death, age, or biographical date-context that this job should have recorded.
Independent review of Liaoshi ch. 042 owned units s0171–s0198 (Mars mid-to-end synodic phases, the Saturn heading and full Saturn synodic table, and Venus from heading through the first prograde-slow segment). Every owned unit is technical calendar-astronomy: daily motion in 分, phase durations in 日, 度 remainders, 留/逆/從/伏, and 一終 cycle lengths. unitPeople is empty for these units and for the adjoining context units. No named person, birth, death, age, reign, era, or personal event is present, so empty ownedItems and ownedPeople is consistent. Numerals such as 九十二日, 十日, 七百八十日, and 日餘/度餘 are planetary intervals and fractional remainders, not historical dates or life-year bounds. 火星, 土星, and 金星 are planet labels, not persons. Context-only neighbors (s0168–s0170, s0199–s0201, s0051) likewise contain no personal chronology that would make the empty ownership incomplete. No itemChecks or personChecks were required. No findings.
Owned units s0199–s0219 are planetary-parameter prose with no named persons, births, deaths, ages, or dated life events. Personal chronology is confined to s0220–s0223 (plus supplied s0232). s0220 dates Heng’s own memorial against He Chengtian’s calendar to 梁武帝天監三年; Academia Sinica (Julian before 1582) places that lunisolar year at 504-02-01 to 505-01-20, so the conventional year AD 504 is the correct label and must not be expanded into a 504–505 window. s0221’s 九年正月 is the same 天監 era: the edict adopting 祖沖之’s 《甲子元曆》 is Emperor Wu’s own act. Sinica gives 天監九年正月 as 510-01-26 to 510-02-23 Julian; a two-day proleptic-Gregorian adjustment stays inside AD 510, so westernYear 510 is valid for that month. 南齊書 records 祖沖之 died 永元二年 (conventional AD 500); 宋書 places 何承天’s death after the 元嘉二十四年 dismissal (conventional AD 447). Both reception claims dated 504/510 are therefore posthumous references, not living activity, and must not feed life dates or active hints. s0223 names 聖宗’s use of 賈俊’s calendar; s0232 supplies 聖宗統和十二年. Sinica spans that Chinese year 994-02-13 to 995-02-02 Julian; the conventional year remains AD 994. Hints AD 510 (武帝’s edict) and AD 504 (恒’s memorial) match supported personal events; 何承天 correctly has no active hint. No owned unit attests birth, death, or age for p011–p013, and none should be invented from this chapter.

itemChecks.event: Emperor Taizong collected Jin officials, retainers, artisans, and calendrical specialists from Bianjing and moved them to the Central Capital in Datong 1.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is p002 (太宗). s0228 dates that collection-and-relocation to 大同元年. Liao Taizong’s Datong era is confined to AD 947 (second through ninth months); a year-only conventional label therefore maps to westernYear AD 947 and does not require a one-sided bound or a second invented endpoint. The source does not give month or day for this act.

evidence.quote: 大同元年，太宗皇帝自晉汴京收百司僚屬伎術歷象，遷於中京，遼始有歷。

itemChecks.event: Ma Chongji, Later Jin Director of Astronomy, presented the Yiwei Origin Calendar, titled the Tiaoyuan Calendar, in Jin Tianfu 4.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is p003 (馬重績). s0230 dates his 奏上 to 晉天福四年, i.e. Later Jin Gaozu’s Tianfu, year 4, whose conventional Western year is AD 939 (Tianfu 1 opened in AD 936). This is Ma’s own Jin-court presentation, not Taizong’s later capture of the same calendar. Year-only precision is appropriate.

evidence.quote: 晉天福四年，司天監馬重績奏上《乙未元曆》，號《調元曆》，太宗所收天汴是也。

itemChecks.event: Wang Bai of the Directorate of Astronomy submitted a calendar in Muzong’s Yingli 11.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is p005 (王白). s0231 names 司天王白 among those who 進歷 in 穆宗應歷十一年. Liao Muzong’s Yingli 1 began in AD 951; Yingli 11 is the conventional year AD 961. The endpoint dates Wang Bai’s submission, not activity across the whole Yingli reign.

evidence.quote: 穆宗應歷十一年，司天王白、李正等進歷，蓋《乙未元曆》也。

itemChecks.reason: Owner is p006 (李正). The same s0231 sentence jointly dates 李正’s participation in the Yingli 11 submission. Conversion of 應歷十一年 to AD 961 follows Muzong’s Yingli count (year 1 = 951). Joint presentation is still Li Zheng’s own dated act.

evidence.quote: 穆宗應歷十一年，司天王白、李正等進歷，蓋《乙未元曆》也。

itemChecks.event: Jia Jun, prefect of Kehanzhou, presented a new calendar identified as the Great Brightness Calendar in Shengzong’s Tonghe 12.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is p008 (賈俊). s0232 dates 賈俊進新歷 to 聖宗統和十二年. Shengzong’s Tonghe 1 began in AD 983; Tonghe 12 is the conventional year AD 994. s0233 independently confirms a Tonghe 12 promulgation. Year-only precision matches a reign-year label without month or day.

evidence.quote: 聖宗統和十二年，可汗州刺史賈俊進新歷，則《大明曆》是也。
高麗所誌《大遼古今錄》稱統和十二年始頒正朔改歷，驗矣。

itemChecks.event: Emperor Shengzong adopted Jia Jun’s newly presented calendar and issued it under the old Song Daming name.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is p007 (聖宗). s0223 states 聖宗以賈俊所進新歷…行之, which is Shengzong’s own adoption. The year is not in that sentence; s0232 dates Jia Jun’s presentation to 統和十二年 and owned s0233 confirms 統和十二年始頒正朔改歷. Combining those passages supports AD 994 as the conventional year of adoption/promulgation, not a dynasty-long window. Certainty explicit is acceptable because both the act and the Tonghe 12 promulgation are source-stated.

itemChecks.event: Zu Chongzhi presented the Jiazi Epoch Calendar methods, later called the Great Brightness Calendar, in Song Daming 6.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is p001 (祖沖之). s0011 dates 祖沖之上《甲子元曆》法 to 宋武帝大明六年. The temple name 武帝 is the Liao Shi’s label; Liu Song 大明 is Xiaowu’s era (AD 457–464), and 大明六年 is AD 462. Owned s0012’s 宋大明七年癸卯 independently fixes Daming 7 as the 癸卯 year AD 463, so Daming 6 is AD 462 without relying on 武帝. Competing reading of the temple name is preserved by leaving p010 undated (claim-59) rather than moving Zu’s year. Year-only conventional label; no month/day to convert onto the proleptic Gregorian day calendar.

evidence.quote: 宋武帝大明六年，祖沖之上《甲子元曆》法，未及施用，因名《大明曆》。

This is a place attached to that single event, not a claim that Taizong operated at Bianjing throughout a dynasty.
